topics.label: Lecture introduction and aims
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture as bringing previously introduced immune cells and molecules together to explain inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how innate immunity distinguishes infection and damage through molecular patterns and appropriately positioned, germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptors and their signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how toll-like receptors translate microbial recognition into immune responses suited to the location of the infection.

topics.label: Recognition beyond TLRs and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how additional danger-sensing pathways activate inflammation and can contribute to inflammatory disease.

topics.label: Sentinel-cell responses and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow how activated sentinel cells initiate inflammatory responses that bring circulating leukocytes into infected tissue.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells carry evidence of tissue infection through the lymphatic system to initiate adaptive responses in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Excessive inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how an excessive inflammatory response becomes a dangerous systemic process rather than a protective local one.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation is shut down through declining stimulation and active anti-inflammatory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine recovery after tissue damage and why persistent inflammation can become either a source of continuing injury or a means of containing an uncleared infection.

topics.label: Lecture closing and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and identifies complement as the subject of the next lecture.
